## workflow finish

Finish a merged branch: switch to its base, catch the base up, and delete the branch

### Synopsis

Finish the checked-out branch once its pull or merge request has merged: switch
to its base, fast-forward the base with git pull --ff-only, and delete the
branch — the three git commands the interface's F runs. They are printed and
confirmed before any runs, and a step git refuses stops the rest, keeping the
branch.

A branch that cannot be finished is refused with the reason, and exits 4: its
pull or merge request has not merged, it is the base itself or a detached
HEAD, there is no base to return to, or it holds commits that neither merged
nor are on its upstream, which deleting it would lose. The delete is a force
delete, so it goes ahead only for a branch at the very commit that merged, or
one whose upstream holds every commit on it.

```
workflow finish [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  workflow finish --dry-run   # the three git commands, none run
  workflow finish --yes       # finish a merged branch, unattended
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help   help for finish
      --yes    go ahead without the confirmation
```
